metadata.title: Compute.VM Type Class
metadata.description: The VM Type Class — extends the Compute Base Class (cpu/memory/storage/storage_tier/guest_os, inherited) with VM-specific SharedDataElements, under the Liskov invariant (add or refine, never contradict). A provider Class (Compute.VM.OCPVirt, …) extends this further. The generator compiles this class + its ancestors into today's flat Compute.VM resource-type spec.

instance_size.description: Provider-neutral size class (small|medium|large, ordered/comparable — common-elements §2.2, DCM ADR-014). Size by class IN PLACE OF cpu+memory; the provider maps it to concrete resources at naturalization (DCM ADR-023). anyOf enforces sizing by class OR raw.

count.description: Total virtual CPUs. The provider naturalizes this to its native cpu model (a KubeVirt domain cpu, a hypervisor platform's sockets*cores, a public cloud's vCPUs) at realization (DCM ADR-023).

sockets.description: Optional topology hint: sockets. Provider-support-dependent; ignored where not applicable.

cores_per_socket.description: Optional topology hint: cores per socket. Provider-support-dependent.

cpu.description: Redeclared at VM scope to TIGHTEN the base shape (required sub-fields) — tighten at your scope; BareMetalHost keeps the loose base shape verbatim.

size.description: Memory allocation, e.g. 16GB or 16Gi (class-aligned quantity pattern — Compute Base Class `memory.size`).

hugepages.description: Optional huge-page backing (provider-support-dependent; validated against provider capability).

memory.description: Redeclared at VM scope to TIGHTEN the base shape (required sub-fields) — tighten at your scope; BareMetalHost keeps the loose base shape verbatim.

storage.description: The reference-discipline storage requirements descriptor (PVD-001, Compute Base Class shape) — numeric minima the realizing storage must meet. The requested performance class is the governed `storage_tier` element, not an inline enum here.

storage_tier.description: The requested storage performance class — a GOVERNED vocabulary (ADR-038 §2): canonical terms are `storage_tier` reference-data records (standard/performance/archive), each denoting a requirements floor. Name-selectable but requirements-authoritative (ADR-036); profile decides bare string vs data_reference (ADR-007/ADR-039). Mirrors the Compute Base Class `storage_tier` element. Governed vocabulary `storage_tier` (ADR-038 §2); name-selectable but requirements-authoritative (ADR-036). Profile decides bare-vs-reference.

guest_os.description: Guest operating system. Portable form is a reference to an os_image reference-data vocabulary (DCM ADR-012; layering §3.7) the target provider advertises via capability discovery (ADR-PROV-002); policy validates membership at request. Inline is the portability_breaking escape. Optional at the data layer (bare-instantiation philosophy): a VM may be declared by sizing alone; a profile MAY require it.

type.description: Inline OS identifier (e.g. linux-server-9). portability_breaking: a value with no os_image vocabulary entry — a review finding.

firmware.description: Guest firmware surface — portable across every major virtualization stack (Redfish Boot.BootSourceOverrideMode, KubeVirt firmware/TPM, cloud UEFI/trusted-launch). Required by modern guests (Win11-class needs uefi + secure_boot + vtpm). Governed vocabulary `vm_firmware` (ADR-038 §2); name-selectable but requirements-authoritative (ADR-036). Profile decides bare-vs-reference.

type.description: Firmware interface presented to the guest.

secure_boot.description: UEFI Secure Boot. Only valid with type: uefi (policy-validated).

vtpm.description: Virtual TPM 2.0 device presented to the guest.

boot_order.description: Ordered boot device preference (VM-specific; not meaningful for BareMetal or Container).

layout_ref.description: The Storage.Layout this VM realizes — handle/uuid reference to an existing Storage.Layout whose entries describe the VM's disks (per-disk shape, boot designation, storage tier). Common-elements Reference (handle string or {uuid, handle} object), following the location_ref/network_ref precedent. Also carried as a references->Storage.Layout relationship (storage_layout).

networks.description: Network attachment INTENT — name-selectable but requirements-authoritative (ADR-036). Select a network by `network_ref`, or state `zone`/`requires` and let placement converge on one. Neither is required; unstated, policy decides. Explicit requirements are authoritative over a name.

network_ref.description: The Network.VirtualNetwork this interface attaches to — common-elements Reference (handle string or {uuid, handle} object); resolvable, policy-walkable, never an opaque string.

vlan.description: REQUIREMENT — WHICH LOGICAL NETWORK, as a reference to a `Network.VLAN`. The VLAN is the identity of a logical network (maintainer ruling 2026-08-10): a segment id under an encapsulation, which is what an operator means by "put it on that network". Stated when the attachment must land on a specific logical network — because it has to reach something already there, or an existing application lives on it. Absent means policy decides. REALIZATION VARIES; THE AXIS DOES NOT. `Network.VLAN.encapsulation` already carries vlan / vxlan / geneve / flat, so the class is a SEGMENT of which 802.1Q is one form. A public cloud exposes no VLAN — there the segment is a VPC subnet, adopted by reference on Network.VLAN rather than given a parallel class: the VPC is the Network.VirtualNetwork and the subnet is the addressed segment within it. A consumer states the segment; which encapsulation realizes it is the provider's. Resolved against the `segment` relationship a Network.VirtualNetwork already declares, so placement narrows to networks on that segment rather than requiring the consumer to know which provider network carries it.

subnet.description: REQUIREMENT — WHICH IP NETWORK, as a reference to a `Network.Subnet`. Layer 3, and INDEPENDENTLY SELECTABLE from `vlan` (layer 2): a subnet usually sits on a segment, but one segment may carry several subnets and a cloud may expose no segment at all, so the mapping is not concrete (maintainer ruling 2026-08-10). "Put me on 198.51.100.0/24" and "put me on VLAN 3020" are different requests; a consumer may state either, both, or neither.

zone.description: REQUIREMENT — the network CATEGORY this attachment needs (DMZ, management, internal), as a governed taxonomy term. Independent of `vlan` and `tier`: which logical network, what kind of network, and how good it is are three different questions, and a consumer may state any, all, or none of them. FOR PLACEMENT ONLY. Requiring the management zone does not grant access to it, and nothing critical may hang off the category directly — anything required because of a zone is enforced by a policy reading it (maintainer ruling 2026-08-10). A zero-trust posture derives no trust from network location (NIST SP 800-207).

tier.description: REQUIREMENT — the governed `network_tier` (performance) this attachment needs. Independent of `vlan`: which logical network and how good it is are different questions, and a consumer may state either, both, or neither. Each term denotes a floor, so any network meeting it qualifies — name-selectable but requirements-authoritative (ADR-036).

ip_address_ref.description: A pre-allocated Network.IPAddress to bind to this interface (optional — omitted means the address service allocates at realization). Common-elements Reference shape.

placement.description: Placement INTENT expressed as a SELECTION of an existing Facility.Location (populated by a platform data layer and/or a Facility.Location provider), plus affinity relative to other existing resources. Policy governs which locations a given consumer may select; the VM only references one — it does not define locations itself (ADR-009 §4: guidance, not a gate).

location_ref.description: handle/uuid of an existing Facility.Location the VM is placed in — chosen from the eligible set (platform-layer + provider-advertised, policy-filtered). Also carried as a references->Facility.Location relationship.

zone.description: Availability/sovereignty zone constraint, selected from the zones the provider advertises for the chosen location; resolved against that location.

affinity.description: Co-location / separation intent relative to OTHER named resources (not nodes). Each target is resolved at reserve, so a pre-known UUID is not required.

target.description: Handle OR label-selector of an existing resource to co-locate with / avoid, resolved at reserve (ADR-025/AEP-124) - you do not need its UUID in advance.

selector.description: Alternative to a handle: match target(s) by labels (key/value).

run_state.description: Desired guest RUN state the provider drives to (e.g. KubeVirt runStrategy). Distinct from the four-state lifecycle_state; snapshot/restore are separate operations, not run states. The discovered counterpart is outputs.observed_run_state.

spec.description: Deliberate exclusions: GPU/PCI passthrough and SR-IOV are Provider-Class SharedDataElements (ADR-038) — provider-variable capability, not portable base surface. Day-0 guest personalization (cloud-init/user-data) is an open design decision (process concern vs VM field) — tracked on the type, not silently absent. Per-disk shape (sizes, boot designation) lives on Storage.Layout, referenced via layout_ref.

ip_addresses.description: Assigned guest IP addresses (all interfaces), IPv4-first ordering. The canonical binding surface for LB backend pools, DNS records, and monitoring targets.

primary_ip.description: The primary/management address — first of ip_addresses; the single-address convenience most bindings want.

hostname.description: Realized guest hostname (FQDN where the realm provides one).

mac_addresses.description: Realized MAC per interface, ordered as spec.networks[]. Binding surface for DHCP reservation and switch-port records.

provider_handle.description: The provider-native identifier of the realized VM (opaque; correlation/ops use only — never a portable reference).

observed_run_state.description: Observed run state at last reconciliation (running|stopped|suspended) — the discovered counterpart of spec.run_state.desired_state. Renamed from `run_state` (0.7.0) so desired (spec) and observed (outputs) never share a name.

target_segment.description: Realize-time placement fact (ADR-011 two-phase reserve): a reference to the Network.VLAN segment the reserved/realized placement can reach (adopt-not-absorb — the segment id/encapsulation live on the Network.VLAN). This is the declarable binding source for a fulfillment:provider dependency whose criteria are simply the target segment — e.g. a Network.IPAddress allocated on the reachable segment (ADR-009 §3 worked example: bind target_segment -> the IP request's segment_ref). It is a shared-reference fact, NOT the vNIC/MAC/host-networking (those are the VM provider's own internal facts, never cross-provider criteria).

relationships.description: May consume zero or more pre-allocated Network.IPAddress addresses (optional dependency).

relationships.name: placement
relationships.description: Placed in an existing Facility.Location (selected, policy-governed) — see spec.placement.location_ref.

relationships.name: network_attachment
relationships.description: Attaches to existing Network.VirtualNetwork(s) — see spec.networks[].network_ref.

relationships.name: storage_layout
relationships.description: The Storage.Layout this VM realizes — see spec.layout_ref; the layout's entries describe the VM's disks.

relationships.name: disk
relationships.description: Consumes existing/allocated Storage.Volume(s) — the consumable volumes realizing its Storage.Layout entries.

adopts.role: Vendor-neutral compute-system representation spanning physical AND virtual (Redfish ComputerSystem SystemType: Physical | Virtual | Composed | Partitioned) - the single representative standard for the Compute.* family (shared with Compute.BareMetalHost). Provider-NATIVE realizations (KubeVirt, a hypervisor platform, a public cloud, ...) are declared on the provider support matrix, not on the substrate type.
k8s-native VM realization vocabulary (domain cpu/memory, interfaces->networks, volumes, runStrategy/power) — the parallel to Metal3 for bare metal

context.purpose: Declares a virtual machine — sizing, guest OS, storage requirements, network attachments, placement — as portable intent any virtualization provider can realize.
context.plain_description: The request for one VM: how big — a named size class (`instance_size`), or explicit `cpu` and `memory` in its place — what `guest_os`, what storage it needs (`storage` minima and a governed `storage_tier`), which Storage.Layout describes its disks (`layout_ref`), and which existing networks its NICs attach to (`networks`, each entry naming a `network_ref`). Placement is a selection of an existing location, not an invention. Once the provider builds it, the record carries realized facts back: IP addresses, hostname, provider handle. The hypervisor (KubeVirt, libvirt, a cloud) is a provider detail, never part of the type.
use_when: You need to request a VM with declared size, OS, storage requirements, and network attachments, portable across hypervisors.
You need VM records in the dependency graph so ordering (host before VM, VM before its services) is derivable.
You need a VM's disk shape and addresses to reference existing Storage.Layout / Network.IPAddress records rather than duplicate them.
not_for: The physical machine it runs on — Compute.BareMetalHost.
A containerized workload — Compute.Container; the VM carries a full guest OS.
The per-disk shape (sizes, boot designation) — Storage.Layout; the VM references one via layout_ref.
The vNIC as a device record — that is Hardware.NetworkInterface with a virtual device_class; the VM's networks list declares attachment intent, not device inventory.
works_with: Storage.Layout — the disk layout the VM realizes (per-disk shape, boot designation).
Network.VirtualNetwork — the networks the VM's NICs attach to.
Storage.Volume — the consumable volumes realizing its layout entries.
Facility.Location — where the VM is placed (selected from existing places, policy-governed).
Network.IPAddress — pre-allocated addresses the VM consumes.
